newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-election skitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-election skitters.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates was up 95 basis points to 21.50 percent in early trade on Wednesday due to what dealers said was market tension ahead of forthcoming mid-term elections.
"Rates are under a little pressure due to speculation on pre-election jitters," a trader said.

Mexico will hold elections on July 6 to replace the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate and several state governors. It will also elect the Mexico City mayor for the first time in modern history.
Traders said inflation data released late on Tuesday were having an exaggerated impact on a nervous market, although consumer prices rose by only slightly more than expected.
"Inflation came out a little more than we were expecting, and that did not go down well. Anything can move this market right now," the trader added.

Banco de Mexico announced the consumer price index had risen by 0.49 percent during June 1-15. A previously conducted Reuters survey MEX22 of 13 financial houses showed they had forecast an average rise of 0.47 percent.
Dealers said secondary market rates were also under pressure due to demand for liquidity to square books for month's end.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile up 30 basis points at 22.50 percent.
Liquidity of 300 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
